title: Lock manager in shared memory
caption: Backend A (the waiter) asks the shared lock table for a lock held by Backend B, queues, and is woken by a latch; the deadlock check only aborts someone if it finds a cycle.

badges.meaning: Postmaster creates shared memory
Backend joins ProcArray
Tries a weak lock via fast-path slots
Requests a lock in the lock hash table
Conflict, so it joins the wait queue
After a timeout the deadlock check runs
Only if a cycle exists, a victim is aborted
Holder releases its locks
Lock manager sets the waiter's latch
Latch wakes the waiting backend

title: One table lock conflict
caption: Follow the arrows down: A takes the lock, B asks and must wait, the deadlock check finds no cycle, then A's commit wakes B.

badges.meaning: Backend A runs ALTER TABLE and requests AccessExclusiveLock
Lock manager grants it
Backend B's SELECT wants AccessShareLock
Conflict is detected
B sleeps in the wait queue
After 1s the deadlock check finds no cycle
A commits and releases all locks
Lock manager grants B and wakes it
B's SELECT runs

title: Anatomy of the lock table
caption: A LOCKTAG hashes to one of 16 partitions and keys a LOCK; PROCLOCKs link each LOCK to the PGPROCs holding or waiting for it.

badges.meaning: LOCKTAG identifies the locked object and is hashed to a partition
The hash code picks one of 16 partitions
LOCK, one per locked object
PROCLOCK, one per holder
LOCALLOCK, the backend's private copy
